narr: Afternoon showers and thunderstorms produced widespread heavy rain over north and central Georgia on the evening of July 19th and 20th. Rainfall amounts ranged from 1 to 3 inches, with pockets of 3 to 5 inches over northeast Georgia and the Atlanta metro area. As a result, flash flooding occurred, including several reports of water rescues. These rainfall amounts occurred during a prolonged persistent period of abundant moisture, with several back to back days of rainfall saturating soils.
ev: The public reported water flowing over the roadway near Mount Berry Square Mall and Armuchee Connector. Radar estimates indicate that 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, on top of the 1 to 3 inches that fell the day prior. These amounts, falling on the already saturated soils, produced flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Willie Robinson Road washed out due to high flow on Latham Creek. Radar estimates indicate 2 to 3 inches of rain quickly fell on already wet soils from rain that occurred in the preceding few days. This quickly accumulating rainfall resulted in the flash flooding.

A state official reported a road closure due to flash flooding near the intersection of Highway 53 and Calhoun Avenue. Radar estimates indicate that 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, on top of the 1 to 3 inches that fell the day prior. These amounts, falling on the already saturated soils, produced flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported floodwaters from Intrenchment Creek resulted in the water rescue of a person in a vehicle traveling on Constitution Road. The local USGS river gage (NWS INTG1 / USGS 02203700) also observed a rapid rise above Minor flood stage. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the closure of Garden Lakes Parkway near Beech Creek due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, on top of the 1 to 3 inches that fell the day prior. These amounts, falling on the already saturated soils, produced flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a closed road near the intersection of Highway 27 and Old Dalton Road due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over the area, on top of the 1 to 3 inches that fell the day prior. These amounts, falling on the already saturated soils, produced flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported numerous road closures due to flash flooding, including, but not limited to JC Wright Road, Campground Road, Bagwell Road and Smyrna Church Road. Most of these locations experienced flooding due to high flow through a nearby creek or stream. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain fell over the area, on top of the 1.5 to 2.5 inches that fell the day prior.
